intro: Professionals and everyday users convert megabytes (MB) to gigabytes (GB) when working across metric and metric standards in engineering specifications, international trade documentation, and technical measurements. One megabyte (decimal) equals 0.001 gigabytes, while 1 gigabyte (decimal) equals 1,000 megabytes. Whether you are verifying digital storage specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

faqs.question: How many gigabytes (GB) are in 1 megabyte (decimal) (MB)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.001 gigabytes (GB) in 1 megabyte (decimal) (MB), which rounds to 0.001 GB for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 gigabyte (decimal) equals 1,000 megabytes.

faqs.question: How do I convert megabytes to gigabytes (MB to GB)?
faqs.answer: To convert megabytes to gigabytes, use the formula: GB = MB × 0.001. For example, converting 16 MB gives 0.016 GB.

faqs.question: What is 16 megabytes in gigabytes?
faqs.answer: 16 megabytes (MB) equals exactly 0.016 gigabytes (GB) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
